title: Capture-fencing and staggered-replay verifier for multi-stream decode
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Problem: We observed rare but reproducible correctness regressions when recreating CUDA graph captures across concurrent decode streams. Root causes appear to be: (1) capture windows aligning mid-prefill leading to KV-cache epoch mismatches, (2) speculative kernel selection differences between capture and replay paths for short sequence lengths, and (3) in-flight stream interleaving that exposes non-atomic updates to shared tensors. Goal: implement a lightweight capture-fencing protocol plus a staggered-replay verifier to guarantee replay determinism across multi-stream decode without regressing latency for common cases. This ticket covers design, implementation hooks in the runtime capture manager, unit/regression tests, and a controlled rollout.
acceptance_criteria: No correctness regressions observed in the multi-stream regression harness across 100k simulated concurrent prefill+decode sequences
Capture and replay produce byte-for-byte identical KV-cache states and model outputs for deterministic models (seeded) in our replay verifier
P95 decode latency increase < 3% for steady-state workloads after capture-fencing enabled
New runtime guards default to opt-in for Dedicated customers and opt-out flag for Hosted until rollout is validated
Comprehensive test-suite added to CI with fast-mode and long-running stress-mode
test_plan: unit: capture-fence state transitions (open -> quiesce -> sealed -> replayable)
integration: harness with 64 concurrent streams, varied prefill lengths (1..2048), and randomized kernel selection seeds
regression: run existing graph-recapture tests plus new epoch-fence scenarios nightly (30m stress)
fuzz: mutate prefill alignment offsets to validate fence boundaries and assert no index corruption
perf: A/B test against baseline for P50/P95/P99 latency with 100k tokens synthesized workload
rollout_plan: feature-flag gate: runtime.capture_fence = off by default in Hosted, on by default in Dedicated staging clusters
canary: enable capture_fence on 10% of Dedicated capacity for 72 hours with tight monitoring
verify: run staggered-replay verifier against canary logs; if any mismatch, automatic rollback of flag
gradual: increase to 50% then 100% over two weeks after zero regressions
fallback: if regressions or latency spikes > 5% observed, switch to conservative mode (fence only long prefill sequences > 128 tokens)
postmortem: collect and store graph traces and prefill metadata in S3 bucket s3://redwood-debug/graph-traces/ENG-174210
implementation_notes: Introduce CaptureFence object that attaches to graph captures, tracking epoch_id, last_prefill_seq_len, and kernel_profile_hash
On capture start: if other streams share GPU context, try to align fence window to nearest quiesce boundary; otherwise, attach lightweight epoch token to capture
During replay: verify epoch token and kernel_profile_hash; if mismatch, trigger safe-fallback to interpreter path for that stream and emit diagnostic event
Extend kernel selection API to expose stable profile hashes so captures are self-describing and comparable during replay
Optimize common path: rapid-commit fence no-op for single-stream captures to avoid added latency
tradeoffs: Stronger fencing increases correctness but can add small latency for capture-heavy workloads
Conservative fallback (interpreter path) protects correctness but costs tokens; we prefer targeted fallback restricted to mismatched streams
Adding profile hashes increases capture metadata size; we cap at 128 bytes and hash canonicalized kernel config only
Opt-in vs opt-out: opting to be conservative in Hosted reduces customer exposure but slows validation pace
